reply.shortGloss: to take; to catch; to get
reply.emotion: helpful and ready, reaching out a hand to assist
notes: Prendere is one of the most common verbs in Italian, used for physical grasping, catching public transport, and ordering food or drink.
Do not confuse it with portare (to bring/carry), which focuses on movement toward somewhere else rather than the initial act of getting hold of the item.

senses.definition: To take hold of something with your hands and move it or pick it up.

examples.text: Ho deciso di prendere la borsa e uscire.
examples.translation: I decided to take the bag and go out.
examples.emotion: decisive and ready, moving with purpose

senses.definition: To catch something that is moving towards you, such as a ball or an object thrown in the air.

examples.text: Cerca di prendere la palla prima che cada.
examples.translation: Try to catch the ball before it falls.
examples.emotion: urgent and encouraging, focused on a fast-moving object

senses.definition: To board or catch a means of transport like a train, bus, or plane.

examples.text: Domani mattina devo prendere il treno per Roma.
examples.translation: Tomorrow morning I have to catch the train to Rome.
examples.emotion: organized and a little rushed, thinking about the journey ahead

senses.definition: To order food or drink at a bar, restaurant, or cafe.

examples.text: Voglio prendere un caffè prima di iniziare a lavorare.
examples.translation: I want to have a coffee before starting to work.
examples.emotion: relaxed and looking forward to a pleasant break

definitions: To take hold of something with your hands and move it or pick it up.
To catch something that is moving towards you, such as a ball or an object thrown in the air.
To board or catch a means of transport like a train, bus, or plane.
To order food or drink at a bar, restaurant, or cafe.
